subject: RE: Order Form — Discount ramp, clawback mechanics, and billing alignment
messages:
From: Emily Scott <emily.scott@healthgrid.com>
To: logan_wright@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@healthgrid.com
Date: Sun, 6 Jul 2025 16:10:00 -0400
Subject: Order Form — Exhibit C redlines (discount ramp / clawback / billing)

Logan,

Attached is our redline to Exhibit C and the Order Form. A few of our counterpoints you should expect from legal/procurement so we can move to signature:

- True-up window: we need a full 12 months after the end of the annual term to reconcile usage and apply any credits.
- Clawback: for the ramp discounts in Year 1, we want an explicit clawback if Net Usage across the subscription drops below 80% of the committed baseline in any subsequent 6‑month period.
- Cap on credits: we do not want a hard cap on cumulative credits; we believe uncapped credits protect our financials if usage collapses.
- Escrow: we propose escrow for any advanced discount overpayments (third-party escrow to hold 25% of the upfront discount until the 12-month true-up completes).
- Billing alignment: credits should appear as invoice line items and reduce the following quarter’s invoice; we also asked that SLO-related service credits be netted against the same billing bucket.

Could you please confirm Redwood’s position line-by-line so we can finalize the Order Form? We prefer to have this wrapped before the exec review next Thursday.

Thanks,
Emily
Emily Scott
Director, Procurement — HealthGrid
Procurement Team

Attachment: HealthGrid_Redline_ExhibitC_20250706.pdf (redline PDF, 4 pages)

From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
To: Emily Scott <emily.scott@healthgrid.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 7 Jul 2025 10:02:00 -04:00
Subject: RE: Order Form — Exhibit C redlines (discount ramp / clawback / billing)

Emily — thanks for the clear redline and the list of asks. Looping in Neha (AE), Ben (RevOps) and Laura (Legal) to make sure we give a cohesive response. High-level positions below; we'll follow up with a formal redline/cover note by EOD tomorrow.

Line items:
- True-up window: We understand why you prefer 12 months. Our standard is 9 months to avoid indefinite reconciliation exposure; we can be flexible to 12 months if we get a hard cap on cumulative credits and an objective reconciliation process.
- Clawback on ramp discounts: We can accept a clawback mechanism, but: (a) the trigger needs to be tied to named subscription units / SKUs rather than a broad "Net Usage" definition; (b) the lookback should be quarterly with a 2‑quarter cure before clawback applies to avoid transient dips.
- Cap on credits: We cannot accept unlimited exposure. Proposed cap: 20% of fees paid in the 12‑month period following the ramp (we can discuss whether this is applied annually or as a rolling 12‑month cap).
- Escrow: We do not use third‑party escrow for routine discount true-ups. We are willing to apply credits against future invoices quarterly and provide a reconciliation statement; if you require escrow we would need to understand the scope and costs.
- Billing alignment / SLO credits: Agree that credits should be line items and applied in the next invoice cycle; SLO service credits must be separately accounted but may net against the same invoice bucket if both parties agree.

Ask from our side: can you define how HealthGrid will measure the baseline and provide a simple example of the clawback calculation (spreadsheet or sample numbers)? That will speed legal alignment.

Next steps: Laura and Ben will draft a redline that accepts a 12‑month true-up only if the 20% cap is included and the clawback is stabilized with a 2‑quarter cure. Neha — can you confirm commercial willingness? I suggest a 30‑minute call Tues to walk the computation.

Regards,
Logan Wright
Head of Sales — Redwood Inference
(attachments: none in this message)

From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 7 Jul 2025 11:05:00 -04:00
Subject: Internal — HealthGrid redline: recommended reply language and concessions

Team — quick internal coordination before we send the formal reply to HealthGrid. Keep the legal asks tight; procurement will push for unconditional 12 months and escrow. My recommendations: 

1) Acceptable concessions (to propose back):
   - True-up: Accept 12 months only if capped at 20% of fees for the reconciliation period and with a prescribed reconciliation template.
   - Clawback: Accept but require (i) definition limited to named accounts/SKUs; (ii) trigger after two consecutive underperformance quarters; (iii) clawback limited to applied discounts (not a penalty).
   - Billing: No escrow. Offer quarterly netting of credits against invoices; provide a reconciliation statement with line items.

2) Non-starters / escalation points:
   - No hard unlimited credits — escalate to me/finance if they push.
   - Escrow increases procurement complexity and legal fees — our default is internal accounting offsets.

3) Draft language to include in the redline: short, formulaic definitions for baseline, period, and the clawback math. I’ll ask Ben to draft an example calculation with three tiers (ramp band Year 1, post-ramp baseline, and clawback cap).

Neha — confirm whether the AE is comfortable closing if we hold to 20% cap and remove escrow. If not, what is the maximum we can entertain?

Ben — please draft the sample reconciliation spreadsheet and one-sentence plain-English summary for procurement.

Laura — please propose legal redline language for the cap/true-up/clawback that we can send back.

Thanks — I want to be firm but keep momentum.

— Logan

From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
To: Emily Scott <emily.scott@healthgrid.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 8 Jul 2025 09:22:00 -04:00
Subject: RE: Order Form — Exhibit C redlines (discount ramp / clawback / billing)

Emily — thanks again for the redline. Attached is our response document and a short sample reconciliation that shows how the true-up and any clawback would be calculated (3-sheet example + plain-English summary). Short summary of our positions for clarity: 

1) True-up window: We will accept a 12‑month true-up (per your ask) provided the cumulative credit exposure is capped at 20% of total fees invoiced for the reconciliation period. We propose the cap be applied on a rolling 12‑month basis.

2) Clawback mechanics: We will accept a clawback tied to the named subscription units/SKUs listed on the Order Form. Triggering the clawback requires two consecutive quarters of performance below the baseline and HealthGrid will have a 45‑day cure period after notice before any chargeback is assessed. Clawback amounts are limited to recovered discount amounts, not additional penalties.

3) Escrow: We cannot agree to third‑party escrow for routine true-ups. Instead, Redwood will apply any overpaid discounts as credits against future invoices on a quarterly cadence and will provide an audited reconciliation statement at the end of the 12‑month period.

4) Billing & SLO credits: All credits (true-up credits and SLO service credits) will appear as invoice line items. SLO credits will be separately identified but may be applied to the same invoice bucket if both sides agree.

Next steps: Attached are: (a) Redwood_Response_Concessions_20250707.docx (cover note + redline excerpt); (b) HealthGrid_Trueup_Example.xlsx (sample calculation). If HealthGrid is good with those bullets, please confirm and we’ll publish a clean Order Form for signature. If you want to walk through the spreadsheet, I’m available Tue 3–4pm ET or Wed 10–11am ET.

Best,
Logan Wright
Head of Sales — Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_Response_Concessions_20250707.docx; HealthGrid_Trueup_Example.xlsx
